t: Aim and plan of the session
n: The topic of this session: analysis of anti-inflammatory drug substances. The aim is to familiarise students with the toxicological significance and the methods of analysis of the drugs diclofenac, indometacin and ibuprofen. According to the plan, we will consider the toxicological significance of these three agents and their methods of analysis.

By the end of the session, students master the conditions for detecting the drugs diclofenac, indometacin and ibuprofen in pure solutions and for carrying out qualitative reactions. They perform colour reactions with Liebermann, Mandelin and Marquis reagents and compare the colours. They also determine Rf values in thin-layer chromatography and maxima in ultraviolet spectrophotometry.

Items needed for the work: test tubes, separating funnels, reagents and visual aids. The session is held in a room equipped with special laboratory facilities. For thin-layer chromatography a chromatographic plate and a chamber filled with a chloroform:methanol 9:1 mixture are needed. In ultraviolet spectrophotometry, 96% ethyl alcohol is used as the reference solution.

Reagents are prepared in three groups. For colour reactions, Liebermann reagent, Mandelin reagent and Marquis reagent are needed. For thin-layer chromatography the solvent system is chloroform:methanol 9:1, and the developing reagent is Marquis reagent. For ultraviolet spectrophotometry, 96% ethyl alcohol is used.

Rules of safety and preparation. For the laboratory work the student brings rubber gloves, a wipe and a face mask. The examination is carried out in rooms with ventilation and a fume cupboard, which are locked and sealed when the work is finished. Objects from infected persons, that is those with tuberculosis, hepatitis and AIDS, arrive in a special container and are noted in the documents.

Let us classify today's substances. Diclofenac and ibuprofen are phenylacetic acid derivatives. Indometacin is an indole-3-acetic acid derivative. Ketoprofen and piroxicam are also analysed. All belong to the group of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. That is, by structure they fall into three groups: phenylacetic acid derivatives, an indole-3-acetic acid derivative, and other agents.

Let us talk about the danger of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or NSAIDs for short. One of their most dangerous effects is complete kidney failure. They accumulate in the kidneys and lead to the accumulation of other drugs in the kidneys as well. Elderly patients require particular attention. Even short-term use disturbs the function of the gastrointestinal tract, kidneys and liver and poses a serious threat to life.

The signs of NSAID poisoning are many. Severe abdominal pain, flatulence, sometimes bloody vomiting or bloody urine, gastric ulcer and heartburn are observed. Blood pressure rises, and tachycardia and chest pain appear; platelet production is disturbed and there is a risk of bleeding. Severe headache, dizziness, insomnia, depression, darkening of vision and tinnitus may occur. Severe renal failure, nephritis, swelling of the legs, allergic reactions, hair loss and photosensitisation are also seen.

Let us summarise the signs of poisoning by organ. In the gastrointestinal tract, severe abdominal pain, flatulence, bloody vomiting or bloody urine and gastric ulcer are observed. In the heart and blood vessels, pressure rises, tachycardia occurs, platelet production is disturbed and a risk of bleeding appears. In the kidney, severe renal failure and nephritis develop. In the nervous system, dizziness, insomnia and depression are observed.

Let us look at the maximum daily doses. For ibuprofen it is 2400 mg, for naproxen 1250 mg. Indometacin is 200 mg, and piroxicam 30 mg. For diclofenac sodium it is 150 mg, for ketoprofen 3000 mg. The table gives the doses of ibuprofen, indometacin, diclofenac sodium and ketoprofen in milligrams.

The maximum daily doses in figures. Ibuprofen 2400 mg, naproxen 1250 mg, indometacin 200 mg. Piroxicam 30 mg, diclofenac sodium 150 mg, ketoprofen 3000 mg. This means that the maximum daily doses of the drugs differ. The largest value is for ketoprofen, 3000 mg, and the smallest for piroxicam, 30 mg.

t: A case of self-poisoning with ibuprofen
n: A case of self-poisoning with ibuprofen. The book describes a case in which a patient died as a result of taking a large amount of ibuprofen for the purpose of self-poisoning. Death occurred from failure of the cardiovascular system. Perforation of gastric ulcers and acute inflammatory conditions were also recorded.

Description of diclofenac. Its chemical name is 2-[(2,6-dichlorophenyl)amino]phenylacetic acid, with a molecular mass of 296.2. Diclofenac sodium is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug with anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antipyretic action. It is a phenylacetic acid derivative. Synonyms: Voltaren, Diclac, Diclobene, Diclofen, Ortofen and others.

Chemical and physical indicators of diclofenac. Chemical name 2-[(2,6-dichlorophenyl)amino]phenylacetic acid, molecular mass 296.2. The melting point of diclofenac sodium is 283-285 °C, the dissociation constant pKa=4.2. The partition coefficient in the octanol/water system is 4.5. The substance is soluble in water, and the pH of the medium is 5.2.

Trade names. Synonyms of diclofenac: Voltaren, Diclac, Diclobene, Diclofen, Ortofen and others. Synonyms of ibuprofen: Nurofen, Brufen, Ibufac, Ibufem and others. Synonyms of indometacin: Indocid, Indobene, Metindol, Elmetacin. The expert must know these names in their work, because one substance occurs under different trade names.

Physicochemical properties and pharmacokinetics of diclofenac. Diclofenac sodium is a crystalline powder with a melting point of 283-285 °C; it dissolves well in water at pH 5.2, and also in methanol, acetone, acetonitrile and cyclohexane. The dissociation constant is pKa=4.2, and the partition coefficient in the octanol/water system is 4.5. After a 100 mg retard tablet, the blood concentration is at a maximum at 4 hours, at 0.5 µg/ml. 99% is bound to plasma albumins, and 50% is metabolised in the liver. The half-life is 1-2 hours, and 60% is excreted by the kidneys.

Diclofenac pharmacokinetics in figures. After a 100 mg retard tablet, the blood concentration is at a maximum at 4 hours, at 0.5 µg/ml. 99% is bound to plasma albumins, and 50% is metabolised in the liver. The half-life is 1-2 hours. 60% is excreted by the kidneys.

Ibuprofen. Chemical name 1-methyl-4-(2-methylpropyl)phenylacetic acid, molecular mass 206.3. A white crystalline powder with a melting point of 75-77 °C. Practically insoluble in water, it dissolves well in ethyl alcohol, chloroform and diethyl ether. Its blood concentration is at a maximum in 1-2 hours, and the half-life is 1.8-2.5 hours. The pharmacological effect appears at amounts of 1200 mg and more. Synonyms: Nurofen, Brufen, Ibufac.

Main indicators of ibuprofen. Chemical name 1-methyl-4-(2-methylpropyl)phenylacetic acid, molecular mass 206.3. A white crystalline powder with a melting point of 75-77 °C, practically insoluble in water. It reaches maximum concentration in the blood in 1-2 hours, with a half-life of 1.8-2.5 hours. The pharmacological effect appears at a dose of 1200 mg and more.

Indometacin. Chemical name 1-(4-chlorobenzoyl)-5-methoxy-2-methyl-1H-indole-3-acetic acid, molecular mass 357.8. It is a white crystalline powder with a yellow-brownish tint; the melting point is 155-162 °C, which is a sign of polymorphism. Practically insoluble in water. The concentration is at a maximum 1-2 hours after administration, and 2-4 hours in the retard form; the half-life is 4-5 hours. Food taken slows absorption, and in suppository form it is absorbed less.

Main indicators of indometacin. Molecular mass 357.8, melting point 155-162 °C, which indicates polymorphism. After administration the concentration is at a maximum in 1-2 hours, and in the retard form in 2-4 hours. The half-life is 4-5 hours. Food slows absorption, and in suppository form the substance is absorbed less.

Let us compare the pharmacokinetics of the three agents. Diclofenac in a retard tablet reaches maximum concentration at 4 hours, ibuprofen at 1-2 hours, and indometacin also at 1-2 hours. The half-life is 1-2 hours for diclofenac, 1.8-2.5 for ibuprofen and 4-5 hours for indometacin. Ibuprofen is rapidly metabolised in the body and excreted. The table gives these values side by side.

Let us compare solubility. Diclofenac sodium dissolves well in methanol, acetone, acetonitrile and cyclohexane. Ibuprofen is practically insoluble in water and dissolves well in ethyl alcohol, chloroform and diethyl ether. Indometacin is also practically insoluble in water; it dissolves in ethyl alcohol, chloroform, diethyl ether and acetone. Remember: ibuprofen and indometacin do not dissolve in water.

Briefly about ketoprofen and piroxicam. Ketoprofen is a white crystalline powder with a melting point of 93-96 °C; it dissolves well in acetone, ethyl acetate, alcohol, chloroform and ether. Piroxicam is a crystalline powder with a melting point of 198-200 °C; it dissolves well in alcohol and in an aqueous alkaline medium, and is practically insoluble in water. In thin-layer chromatography Rf=0.57 for ketoprofen and Rf=0.48 for piroxicam.

Let us compare ketoprofen and piroxicam. Ketoprofen is a white crystalline powder with a melting point of 93-96 °C, and dissolves poorly in water. Piroxicam is a crystalline powder with a melting point of 198-200 °C; it dissolves well in alcohol and in an aqueous alkaline medium. In thin-layer chromatography the Rf of ketoprofen is 0.57 and of piroxicam 0.48. With Liebermann reagent ketoprofen gives brown, and piroxicam reddish yellow.

Reaction with Liebermann reagent. Diclofenac gives a reddish-brown colour. Indometacin gives black. Ibuprofen forms an orange-brown colour. The table shows the colour of each substance, and they can be distinguished from one another by this colour.

Five agents with Liebermann reagent. Diclofenac gives reddish brown, ibuprofen orange-brown. Indometacin gives black. Ketoprofen gives brown, and piroxicam forms reddish yellow. Thus the agents can be compared by colour.

t: Reactions with Mandelin and Marquis reagents
n: Reactions with Mandelin and Marquis reagents. With Mandelin reagent, diclofenac gives brown-red and indometacin grey. With Marquis reagent, diclofenac gives dark brown, and indometacin turns orange. The table gives the results of both reagents for both substances.

Let us summarise the colour reactions of diclofenac and indometacin. With Mandelin reagent, diclofenac gives brown-red and indometacin grey. With Marquis reagent, diclofenac is dark brown and indometacin turns orange. With Liebermann reagent, diclofenac is reddish brown and indometacin black. The results of the three reagents must be assessed together.

Thin-layer chromatography analysis. The solvent system is chloroform:methanol 9:1, and the developing reagent is Marquis reagent. Rf=0.47 for diclofenac, Rf=0.38 for indometacin and Rf=0.54 for ibuprofen. The table gives the Rf values of all three substances, and they are separated by these values.

t: TLC: Rf values of five agents
n: Rf values of the five agents. The system is chloroform:methanol 9:1, and Marquis reagent is used as the developing reagent. Diclofenac Rf=0.47, indometacin Rf=0.38, ibuprofen Rf=0.54. Ketoprofen Rf=0.57, piroxicam Rf=0.48. The lowest value is for indometacin, 0.38, and the highest for ketoprofen, 0.57.

Ultraviolet spectrophotometry. 96% ethyl alcohol is used as the reference solution. Diclofenac absorbs at a maximum at wavelengths of 272 and 275 nm. Indometacin gives a maximum at 278 nm, and ibuprofen at 257, 263 and 272 nm. The table gives the maxima in nanometres.

Ultraviolet maxima in figures. In ultraviolet spectrophotometry, 96% ethyl alcohol is used as the reference solution. Diclofenac absorbs at a maximum at 272 and 275 nm, and indometacin at 278 nm. Ibuprofen gives maxima at 257, 263 and 272 nm.

t: Sequence of analysis in the book
n: The sequence of analysis in the book is as follows. First the colour reaction with Liebermann reagent is carried out. Then the colour reactions with Mandelin and Marquis reagents are performed. After that, thin-layer chromatography analysis is carried out: in the chloroform:methanol 9:1 system, developed with Marquis reagent. Finally, ultraviolet spectrophotometry is applied.

Interpreting the result. In the analysis of alkaloids one does not rely on the result of a single reaction, but applies 2 or more reactions and methods. If the reaction used is not characteristic of the substance under test, the chemist may present one substance as another. During the examination, colour reagents may also give a colour with foreign substances and lead to an erroneous conclusion. Therefore the results are assessed together.

A brief reminder about the TDSIS method. Thermal desorption surface ionisation spectroscopy, TDSIS, is a new, highly sensitive method. It makes it possible to analyse nano-quantities of nitrogen-containing molecules and metabolites, with a precision of 1·10-11 g, without chromatographic separation. The method consists in vaporising the molecules of the substance at a programmed temperature and recording the spectrum on a surface ionisation detector.

Review questions. First: describe the toxicological significance of the drug substances diclofenac, ibuprofen and indometacin. Second: name the substances belonging to the group of anti-inflammatory drugs and write their formulae. Third: which reactions can be used in detecting diclofenac, ibuprofen and indometacin? Fourth: describe their analysis by thin-layer chromatography and by TDSIS.

Conclusion. NSAIDs can cause kidney failure. Maximum daily doses: ibuprofen 2400 mg, indometacin 200 mg, diclofenac sodium 150 mg. In thin-layer chromatography, in the chloroform:methanol 9:1 system, the Rf of diclofenac is 0.47, of indometacin 0.38 and of ibuprofen 0.54. In the ultraviolet spectrum, in 96% alcohol, diclofenac gives maxima at 272 and 275 nm, indometacin at 278 nm, and ibuprofen at 257, 263 and 272 nm.
